ic_name: SD Memory Card (SD Simplified Physical Layer Specification)
signaling_summary: All-digital CMOS / LVCMOS signaling on CLK, CMD, DAT0..DAT3. Two normative voltage classes: (1) High Voltage Range (HVR) VDD = 2.7-3.6 V with 3.3 V signaling; (2) Low Voltage Range (LVR) / UHS-I 1.8 V signaling after a successful CMD11 voltage switch sequence. UHS-II uses LVDS differential signaling on a separate pin row (out of scope of the 1-row SD pad assignment). Bus signal load and electrical parameters are defined in Section 6 (Bus Operating Conditions for 3.3 V signaling) and 6.7 (Driver Strength and Bus Timing for 1.8 V signaling).

voltage_classes.applicable_modes: Default Speed, High Speed, SDR12, SDR25 (UHS-I startup), SPI mode

notes: Although the SD bus is digital, the SD Memory Card is fundamentally a flash storage device whose internal NAND array, charge-pump, and read-margining circuitry are highly analog. Those internal analog details are intentionally out of scope of this Physical Layer Specification, which deals only with the host-card interface.
